sales_001:n1.prompt:
You are helping me set up a new CRM account in {{vendor}} as the first step of configuring our sales pipeline. Please do the following:

1. Ask me for any missing information you need before starting: our company/legal name, primary business domain, the email address to use for the account, and the name(s) of anyone with authority to accept vendor terms on behalf of the company.
2. Navigate to {{vendor}}'s signup page and begin the account creation form using our company name, domain, and email address.
3. Fill in all standard account setup fields (company details, industry, team size, etc.) using the information provided, making reasonable placeholder entries only where information is clearly non-binding (e.g., number of employees) and flagging anything you're unsure about.
4. Prepare a short summary of the pipeline stages, key contact/deal properties, and email template categories we'll likely want once the account is live, based on a standard sales pipeline (e.g., New Lead, Contacted, Qualified, Proposal Sent, Closed Won/Lost), so we're ready to move fast once the account exists.
5. When you reach the point where {{vendor}}'s Terms of Service and Data Processing Agreement must be accepted to finalize the account, stop. Do not click accept, agree, or submit on any contractual terms. Present me with a summary of what's been filled in, what remains, and the exact screen/step where approval is needed.

Done looks like: the signup form is fully populated and ready, and you have clearly identified the point requiring my explicit approval. Please stop for human sign-off before finalizing account creation, and report back with a summary of what was completed, any open questions, and the pipeline/property/template plan you prepared for the next configuration step.

sales_001:n2.prompt:
You are helping me configure the deal pipeline in {{vendor}}, our CRM. Before doing anything, ask me for: (1) my {{vendor}} account/domain details if needed, (2) the sales motion(s) we run (e.g., one product line or multiple distinct motions requiring separate pipelines), and (3) the stage names and order I want for each pipeline (or ask me to confirm a sensible default set like Prospecting, Qualified, Proposal Sent, Negotiation, Closed Won, Closed Lost if I don't have preferences).

Using your configured credentials, connect to {{vendor}} via its official API or MCP server if available. Then:
- Draft the full pipeline configuration: pipeline name(s), ordered stage list per pipeline, and whether we need multiple pipelines for different products/motions.
- Confirm the draft supports visual, drag-and-drop stage tracking (a core capability of the product) and note if multi-pipeline support requires a specific plan tier.
- Prepare a clear before/after summary showing exactly what will be created or changed (pipeline names, stages, order) — do not apply any changes yet.

Because this step requires a human to explicitly approve changes before they are applied, present the prepared configuration to me as a checklist/summary and then stop for human sign-off. Do not create, submit, or activate the pipeline in {{vendor}} until I explicitly approve it.

Once I approve, apply the changes via the API/MCP or note precisely which dashboard steps to take if API access isn't available, then verify the pipeline and stages now exist as configured. Report back with: the final pipeline structure created, confirmation it's visible/usable in the {{vendor}} UI, and any limitations encountered (e.g., plan restrictions on multiple pipelines).

sales_001:n3.prompt: You are helping me configure custom contact properties in {{vendor}}, the CRM we've selected, as part of setting up our sales CRM pipeline. If you don't already know it, ask me for: (1) the {{vendor}} account/workspace domain or login URL, (2) the list of custom properties we need (property name, data type e.g. text/number/date/dropdown, and any dropdown option values), and (3) whether these properties should live on the standard Contacts object or a custom object we've defined. Once you have this, using my configured credentials, do the following: log into {{vendor}} (or use its API if available), navigate to the object/property or metadata management area, and create each custom property with the correct field type, label, and any option values I specified. If {{vendor}} supports a documented API for schema/metadata management, prefer using it to create the fields programmatically for accuracy and speed; otherwise use the admin UI. After creating the properties, verify each one appears correctly on the target object by checking the object's field list or opening a sample contact record to confirm the new fields render as expected. If {{vendor}} supports filtered/sorted views, optionally set up one view that surfaces the new properties so the sales team can confirm them at a glance — but do not build the full pipeline or email templates as part of this step. When done, report back: the full list of properties created (name, type, object), confirmation that each one is visible/functional in the CRM, any properties that failed to create along with the error encountered, and whether you used the API or the UI. Flag any properties I requested that aren't supported by {{vendor}}'s field types so I can decide on a workaround.

sales_001:n4.prompt:
You are helping me set up email templates inside {{vendor}}, our CRM, as part of configuring our sales pipeline. Before starting, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available, such as: my {{vendor}} account access confirmation (use your configured credentials), the sales stages or pipeline steps we've already defined, the types of outreach we need templates for (e.g., initial outreach, follow-up, meeting request, proposal follow-up, thank-you/close), any brand voice or tone guidelines, our sender name/signature block, and any placeholder/merge fields we use (like first name, company name, deal stage).

Once you have this, draft the full set of email templates as text (subject line + body for each), using {{vendor}}'s templated email or sequence conventions in words — do not invent API endpoints. Map each draft template to the appropriate pipeline stage or use case. If {{vendor}} supports a documented public API for creating templates programmatically, note that this is possible and describe in words how it would be done, but do not execute any creation or write action yet.

Compile all drafted templates into a single clear summary document (or checklist) showing: template name, purpose/stage, subject line, and full body text, ready for review.

Done looks like: a complete, organized draft of all proposed email templates prepared and ready to load into {{vendor}}, with no templates actually created or saved in the CRM yet.

Because a human must explicitly approve before changes are applied, do not create, save, or publish any templates in {{vendor}}. Present the drafts and checklist to me and then stop for human sign-off.

sales_001:n5.prompt:
You are helping me prepare to connect my email inbox (Gmail or Outlook) to {{vendor}}, our CRM, so emails sync two-way and log automatically to the right contact/deal records. This connection requires an OAuth consent flow that only the mailbox owner can approve, so you must prepare everything and then stop for human sign-off — do not attempt to authenticate, grant access, or click through the OAuth consent screen yourself.

Please do the following:
1. Ask me for: my {{vendor}} account domain/login details context (just confirm I'm logged in with configured credentials, don't ask for secrets), which email provider I use (Gmail or Outlook), and the specific mailbox address to be connected.
2. Using your access to {{vendor}}, navigate to the email/inbox connection settings and identify the exact steps required to link the mailbox (e.g., which menu, which button, what sync/logging options like 'log emails automatically' or 'sync two-way' will need to be selected).
3. Prepare a short checklist listing: the mailbox to connect, the sync settings I should choose (e.g., two-way sync, auto-logging to matching records, tracking options), and any org-level settings (like which users/teams get inbox access) that I'll need to confirm.
4. Note where in the {{vendor}} interface I will need to click 'Connect' and complete the OAuth login/consent (with MFA if applicable) myself.
5. Stop once the checklist and pre-filled settings are ready — do not initiate or complete the OAuth authorization, enter my email password, or approve any consent screen on my behalf.

Report back with: the checklist of settings, the exact location/menu path in {{vendor}} where I'll complete the connection, and a clear note confirming this remains a human step for me to finish.

sales_001:n6.prompt:
You are helping me import my existing contacts into {{vendor}}, our CRM, as part of setting up the sales pipeline. Before starting, ask me for: (1) the CSV file or export of my contacts (and deals/companies if applicable), (2) my {{vendor}} account access confirmation (assume I have configured credentials), and (3) any specific field-mapping preferences (e.g., which column maps to email, company, deal stage, owner).

Once you have the file, do the following:
1. Inspect the CSV structure and propose a field mapping to {{vendor}}'s contact (and company/deal, if present) properties, flagging any columns that don't map cleanly to existing properties so we can decide whether to create custom properties.
2. Check the data for obvious issues: missing required fields, malformed emails, duplicate rows (same email or company), and rows likely to fail import validation. Summarize row counts and any rows that would be dropped or need fixing.
3. Where {{vendor}} supports duplicate detection against existing CRM records, run or simulate that check and report likely duplicate matches for contacts/companies already in the CRM, proposing a merge strategy that preserves all existing data (owners, history, notes).
4. Prepare the full import (mapped fields, dedupe plan, and any new properties needed) as a ready-to-run configuration, but do NOT execute the import into {{vendor}} yet.
5. Note whether the import can be scripted via {{vendor}}'s public API (e.g., creating contact records programmatically) versus a bulk CSV import feature, and recommend which approach fits our contact count and field complexity.

Deliverable: a clear written summary — mapping table, validation issues found, duplicate/merge plan, and the exact import configuration ready to apply. Then stop for human sign-off before applying any changes to the live CRM.
